cases.question: In the experiments, which baselines is ScreenVLM compared against?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: 5.3 defines both baseline families (Qwen3-VL-2B/8B-Instruct, InternVL3-2B; OmniParser v2, YOLOv11-L, RT-DETRv2); other sections only mention 'baselines' in passing.

cases.question: Which pretrained checkpoint is ScreenVLM initialized from, and why was it chosen?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: Only 4.3 states the Granite Docling initialization and its rationale (document-to-markup pretraining); 5.4 merely refers to 'our initialization strategy (Sect. 4)'.

cases.question: In the structure-aware loss, what weight values are given to tag tokens and location tokens?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: The loss is defined in 4.3 (Eq. 1, no values) and ablated in 5.5, but lambda_tag = 2 and lambda_loc = 2 only appear in the last line of 7.2, a section otherwise about baseline fine-tuning.

cases.question: Which viewport size and navigation timeout are used when rendering pages and standardizing screenshots?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: Only 7.6.1 gives the 1440x900 viewport and the 30 s navigation timeout; 3.2 only says pages are rendered with Playwright.

cases.question: Where do the crawled web pages come from, and how many addresses were collected?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: The Web Crawling paragraph of 3.2 is the only place giving the source: 1 million URLs from the 45 Million Websites dataset (Common Crawl, Alexa Top Sites, public domain lists).

cases.question: What proportion of the screenshots is used for training, validation and testing?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: The 90/5/5 split is only in 3.1, titled Overview; 5.2 gives the test-set size (38.6K) but not the split.

cases.question: How is the pixel-coverage overlap between predicted and ground-truth boxes formally defined?
target_path: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
cases.note: 5.2 describes PageIoU informally and points to Appendix 7.3 for the formal definitions.

cases.question: Which three defenses are used to verify the fused multi-shell decoder?
target_path: Unfolding the Leech Lattice: Fused Multi-Shell Decoding and VRAM Layouts for 2-Bit LLM Weights
cases.note: 2.4 lists the three defenses (bit-exact transcoding, every row against f64 before timing, invariant locks such as the kissing number); other sections only cite the f64 check.

cases.question: How is the gap between the kernel time and its DRAM floor attributed?
target_path: Unfolding the Leech Lattice: Fused Multi-Shell Decoding and VRAM Layouts for 2-Bit LLM Weights
3 VRAM Layouts: the In-VRAM Rate as a Design Axis
cases.note: Only 3.4 breaks the 2.04 ms gap down (0.803 ms latency and occupancy, 0.681 ms payload streaming, then residual decode, shared-memory reads and the class-table gather); the introduction and conclusion only quote the 39%.

cases.question: Where can the code and the quantized 4B model be downloaded?
target_path: Unfolding the Leech Lattice: Fused Multi-Shell Decoding and VRAM Layouts for 2-Bit LLM Weights
cases.note: The GitHub and Hugging Face links are only in 9; References only cites third-party repositories.

cases.question: How were the MMLU questions sampled, and how many per subject?
target_path: Unfolding the Leech Lattice: Fused Multi-Shell Decoding and VRAM Layouts for 2-Bit LLM Weights
cases.note: Only 5 states 2 280 questions, 40 per subject from a fixed seed; Appendix A reuses the same questions without describing the sampling.

cases.question: How long does loading the 4B model take, unfolding included, compared with the f16 weights?
target_path: Unfolding the Leech Lattice: Fused Multi-Shell Decoding and VRAM Layouts for 2-Bit LLM Weights
cases.note: The 122-131 s against 186-188 s load times are only in 6; 2.2 'Unfolding at load time' describes the transcoder but gives no load time.

cases.question: At what SM clock speeds did the L40S and the A100 run during the measurements?
target_path: Unfolding the Leech Lattice: Fused Multi-Shell Decoding and VRAM Layouts for 2-Bit LLM Weights
3 VRAM Layouts: the In-VRAM Rate as a Design Axis
cases.note: The 2520 MHz and 1410 MHz boost clocks are only in 3.5, whose title announces a memory hierarchy, not clocks.
